api: No general API. It is an editor, not a platform.
cons: Requires replacing the editor, not adding to it
Multi-vendor data path complicates vendor review
name: Cursor
pros: Familiar to any VS Code user immediately
files: Full repository context with its own indexing, which is the core of the product.
value: A full editor rather than a plugin, which lets it reason across an entire codebase and apply multi-file changes. Where Copilot completes the line you are typing, Cursor is aimed at the change you are trying to make.
engine: Model-agnostic. Routes to frontier models from multiple vendors, with its own models for fast completion.
latency: Fast for completion. Agentic multi-file work is necessarily slower.

pricing.includes: Privacy mode enforcement, SSO, admin controls

quality: Among the strongest available for substantial code changes. Agentic edits still need genuine review, and confident wrong changes across several files are harder to catch than a single bad line.
tagline: An AI-first code editor built around whole-codebase work rather than autocomplete.
use_cases: Multi-file refactors and feature work across a large repository
Agentic tasks where the tool edits, runs, and iterates
integrations: Forked from VS Code, so most VS Code extensions work
governance_note: Because it routes to multiple third-party model providers, the data path is worth mapping explicitly during vendor review. It is not a single-vendor relationship even though it is a single purchase.
training_optout: A privacy mode prevents code being retained, and business tiers can enforce it across the organization. Verify current terms before regulated code goes near it.
